newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Thai baht soars further offshore.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Thai baht soars further offshore.

text.p: The Thai baht rallied against the dollar to at least a 16-year high in the offshore market in early Wednesday trade as foreign players continued scrambling to cover short baht positions, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 22.300/22.500 in early trade offshore compared with 22.800/23.000 late on Tuesday.

Dealers in Singapore said costly baht funding through the forward swap market and the maturity of one-month forward contracts forced offshore players to go on selling dollars for baht in the spot market.
"Tom/next and swap premiums keep rising. It's not a good idea to borrow baht in the swap market right now," said one dealer at a European bank in Singapore.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium rose to 265/295 satangs per dollar in the offshore market from 150/180 late on Tuesday.
Offshore parties were caught severely short of baht by the Bank of Thailand's decision to curb baht supply outside Thailand last month, dealers said.
The Malaysian ringgit firmed following a news report that Malaysia's central bank had warned local banks not lend money offshore for currency speculators.

"There is talk that Bank Negara has warned various local banks about lending money offshore to speculative funds. BN is using moral suasion, saying it will not be there to bail out these local banks if there was a crisis," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.
The talk gave the ringgit some relief against the dollar but the undertone of the local currency remained soft as it seemed unable to shake off the baht's shadow, dealers said.
"Foreign funds think Malaysia could be the next Thailand and they have been really hurt in Thailand. But fundamentally, the two are not the same," the dealer said.
He expected dollar/ringgit to range between 2.50 to 2.52 within the next month. It was hovering around 2.5095/05 at 0325 GMT.
The Indonesian rupiah firmed against the dollar in moderate early trading on the back of relatively expensive overnight rates, dealers said.
They said the spot market was driven by liquidity while forwards inched up on the tight money market and also on fears of the Thai factor.
"The Thai factor and relatively high overnight rates have driven forwards higher," the dealer said.
Overnight rupiah eased slightly to 14.5 percent from 17.0 percent. One-month swaps edged up to 13.75/14.50 from 13.25/14.00, two to 28.5/20.0 from 26.25/26.75.
One dealer in Singapore said the rupiah came under upward pressure in the tight market, but said he thought the rupiah was likely to hit strong resistance at the 2,425.0 level.
"I think the rupiah is a good sell at the 2,425.0 level. Further upswing is limited by the (intervention) band," he said.
A European bank dealer said local operators were seen taking profits from the forward market although offshore players continued to overborrow the rupiah.
